chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام:
Regarding a man who deliberately broke his fast during the month of Ramadan for one day without any excuse, he said:
"He must free a slave, or fast for two consecutive months, or feed sixty poor people. If he cannot do so, he should give charity according to what he is able."

key_terms.تَصَدَّقَ بِمَا يُطِيقُ: he gives charity according to his ability
key_terms.سِتِّينَ مِسْكِينًا: sixty poor persons to be fed
key_terms.شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: the month of Ramadan, the obligatory month of fasting
key_terms.عُذْرٍ: a valid excuse or legal justification
key_terms.يُعْتِقُ رَقَبَةً: he frees a slave as expiation

ai.seo_question: What is the kaffarah for deliberately breaking a fast in Ramadan without an excuse?
ai.summary: This hadith gives the legal expiation for one who deliberately breaks a day of fasting in the month of Ramadan without a valid excuse. It lists the kaffarah options of freeing a slave, fasting two consecutive months, or feeding sixty poor people, and if unable, giving charity according to one's capacity.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1884 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdullah (as), regarding a man who deliberately broke his fast during the Month of Ramadan for one day without any excuse.
Imam (as) said: "He must free a slave, or fast for two consecutive months, or feed sixty poor people. If he cannot afford any of these, he should give charity to the extent of his ability."
